'''Paula K. Hagedorn Diehr''' is an American [[biostatistics|biostatistician]] whose research topics generally concern [[health system]]s and [[ageing]], and have included work on [[spatial variability]] and [[longitudinal data]],{{r|biostat}} health care utilization, [[mental health]], [[insurance]], [[diagnosis]],{{r|hserv|mudd}} and prediction of healthy life expectancies.{{r|hserv|prime}} She is a [[professor emerita]] of biostatistics, with a joint appointment in health systems and population health, at the [[University of Washington]].{{r|biostat|hserv}}

==Education and career==
Diehr graduated from [[Harvey Mudd College]] in 1963.{{r|mudd}} She went to the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] for graduate study, earning a master's degree and Ph.D. in biostatistics there.{{r|biostat|mudd}} Her 1970 doctoral dissertation, ''The Mixture Problem in Tiny Samples'', was supervised by [[Wilfrid Dixon]].{{r|mg}} She joined the [[University of Washington]] faculty in 1970.{{r|mudd}}

==Recognition==
Diehr was named a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 1994,{{r|fasa}} a Fellow of the Association for Health Services Research in 1996,{{r|cwoc}} and a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 1997.{{r|aaas}}

In 2013 Harvey Mudd College gave her their HMC Outstanding Alumni Award.{{r|mudd}}
